basis: Chronic intertwin blood transfer causes fetal anemia and polycythemia; the disease directly affects blood despite its obstetric classification.
Acute gonococcal infection of the urinary bladder.
Inherited amyloid protein disorder; neuropathy and cardiomyopathy each affect substantial shares (>30%). Renal damage varies by subtype and is not consistently >=30% across the umbrella.
Lymphoid proliferation ranging to lymphoma defines PTLD. Specific extranodal organ damage is variable; supplied hepatic, lung and intestinal findings are occasional.
Immunodeficiency with ectodermal dysplasia; motor delay 4/4 and speech delay 5/5 support neurologic involvement; conical teeth reported in 1/1 support oral involvement, with limited sampling.
Gonococcal infection commonly involves the urethra, part of the urinary axis. Cervical and other reproductive sites have no axis; disseminated organ disease is uncommon.
Hereditary skeletal myopathy characterized by giant abnormal mitochondria; no supplied evidence establishes a separate metabolic defect or common extra-muscular damage.
Structural malformation of cerebral capillaries defines a vascular disorder located in the brain.
Burkholderia pseudomallei infection; direct pulmonary infection, pneumonia and lung abscess are frequent (30-79%). Other listed organ infections are occasional or very rare.
Retinal malignancy involving both eyes; pineal involvement occurs in a minority and does not qualify.
Keratinopathic ichthyosis with severe hyperkeratosis and keratoderma; flexion contractures are frequent (30-79%). Secondary skin infections do not establish an immune disorder.
Deficiency of the exocrine pancreatic digestive enzyme precursor trypsinogen causes impaired intestinal protein digestion.
Primary degeneration of the optic nerve, included within the ocular axis.
Premature activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal endocrine axis; an underlying CNS lesion is a separate causal disease.
Primary carcinoma arising in the thyroid, an endocrine gland.
Psychiatric body dysmorphic disorder concerning perceived muscularity; no intrinsic muscle damage is defined.
Skeletal dysplasia with vertebral abnormalities and early generalized osteoarthritis; no extra-skeletal involvement is established for this subtype.
Ependymal glial tumor arising within the central nervous system.
Isolated congenital ocular malformation with iris deficiency and frequent additional eye abnormalities; systemic involvement is excluded by the concept.
Severe developmental delay, lipodystrophy and endocrine/lipid defects; cataract 1/1. Cap omits hepatic injury, contractures, thrombocytopenia and pericardial effusion, each reported in 1/1.
Skin atrophy defines acrogeria; joint hypermobility 80-99% and scoliosis 30-79% support musculoskeletal involvement; intellectual disability 30-79% supports neurologic involvement.
Constriction of the penile foreskin is a reproductive organ disorder; urinary tract damage is not intrinsic to the concept.
Intellectual disability and characteristic dental/palatal defects define the syndrome; osteoporosis and tibial bowing each reported in 1/1 support skeletal involvement, with limited sampling.
Inherited retinal dystrophy; the supplied phenotype does not establish extraocular damage.
Acute myeloid malignancy of blood and marrow defined by an 11q23.3 translocation; no common additional organ damage is established.
